messages:
Ravi Singh: Quick draft for a 1-page customer-facing ops primer (prefill, batching presets, streaming fallback, renewal signal). Keep it non-technical.
Claire Wu: Nice. Suggest structure: 1) What we do 2) What you can expect 3) Simple checks 4) How we escalate.
Ravi Singh: Proposed customer opener: 'Well prefill representative prompts, keep a small warm pool for critical flows, and switch to short polling if streaming degrades. We monitor simple signals and will reach out proactively.'
Ben Ortiz: Add three ENG presets (latency / balanced / cost):
- Latency: batch_window_ms=50, max_batch_tokens=512
- Balanced: batch_window_ms=150, max_batch_tokens=2048
- Cost: batch_window_ms=300, max_batch_tokens=4096
Claire Wu: Prefill recipe (customer paste):
```
prefill_enabled: true
prefill_sample: 150
prefill_mode: staggered
warm_pool: 4
warm_pool_ttl_h: 72
```
Ravi Singh: Observability signals (customer-facing names + simple thresholds):
- prefill_success_rate >= 90%
- kv_cache_hit_rate >= 60%
- p95_time_to_first_token_ms < 800
- stream_disconnects_per_10k < 10
Claire Wu: Escalation shortplay: CS runs non-prod repro -> if still failing ENG checks cache keys, model pin, attach trace -> ENG oncall if unresolved.
Ben Ortiz: Short curl for ops (ENG internal):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/fallback -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"mode":"polling","interval_ms":500}'
```
Ravi Singh: Renewal signal to flag: weekly active sessions < 60% expected by day 14 -> schedule health call. Simple email line to customers: 'Were monitoring your instance for 72h post-go-live; reply with 2 example prompts if you see problems.'
runbook-bot: Runbook created: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/cs/prefill-ops-quicksheet (access: customer-success, eng)
